units.scenario: B is Minjun, Nam's Korean friend, met on campus and again after teacher Lee's class. Nam greets him casually and politely, asks how he is, thanks him, asks how to say a Thai word in Korean, and says goodbye and good night the right way.
B is a Korean tutor with hangul flashcards. Nam reads aloud syllables and short words made only of the basic vowels and ㄱ ㄴ ㄷ ㄹ ㅁ (나무, 누구, 오리, 고구마) and asks what they mean.

B is Minjun at a language-exchange party with international students. Nam introduces herself (name, nationality, student), asks where the others are from and which languages they speak, and answers modestly when praised for her Korean.

B is a Korean tutor reading words aloud. Nam says which sound was heard (plain, aspirated or tense: 가/카/까) and reads short words that use every consonant and the compound vowels (포도, 토끼, 아저씨, 시계, 회사).

B is a staff member at a Korean language school in Bangkok, signing Nam up for a class. He asks Nam's age and phone number (a Thai number) and tells Nam the classroom number and the floor; Nam asks his age politely and uses the right number system each time.
B is a waiter at a Korean snack restaurant (분식집) in Bangkok. Nam calls him over, orders popular dishes and drinks, asks for more, says whether the food is spicy, sweet or nutty, and says she is full.

B is a shop assistant in a small Korean stationery and gift shop in Bangkok. Nam asks what colour things are, says which colour and shape she wants (a red heart, a yellow star), and compares items: long or short, heavy or light, the same or different, bright or dark.
B is Minjun at a café table covered with both their things. They point at objects (이게 뭐예요?), ask whose they are, say where they are (on, under, inside, between), and Nam asks to borrow something.

B is a Korean classmate on Nam's first day at a Korean language school. He asks to borrow a pencil or an eraser, asks about the textbook and the homework, they talk about whether Korean is easy, difficult or fun, and they make a card together in class.

B is Minjun on a video call. He asks to see Nam's flat; Nam names the rooms and furniture, says where things are, describes the room (small but clean, quiet) and shows the shoe cabinet and mailbox at the entrance.

B is a Korean friend looking at photos on Nam's phone from a campus festival. He asks who the people are (이분은 누구예요?); Nam says whether they are men, women or children, friends or classmates, what they look like (long or short hair, glasses) and what they do (a cook, a delivery rider, a soldier).

B is a Korean student playing a guessing game with Nam: he says English loanwords the Korean way (컴퓨터, 햄버거, 오렌지, 셀카) and Nam guesses the English word and uses it in a short sentence (N이에요, N 주세요); then they swap roles.

B is the owner of a Korean grocery shop in Bangkok that sells fruit and vegetables. Nam names fruits and vegetables, asks what something is (이게 뭐예요?), says which fruit is the most delicious, and buys a few things (N 주세요).
B is Minjun showing Nam the shops in the Korean Town area of Bangkok. They point at shops (빵집, 서점, 분식집…), say what each shop is and what it sells, and Nam says what she needs there (N 주세요 / N이에요?).

B is a Korean tourist in Bangkok who asks Nam about the signs in a Korean restaurant and a department store with Korean signs. Nam reads signs aloud (나가는 곳, 타는 곳, 공사 중, 휴무…) and checks what they mean or whether it is the right place (나가는 곳이에요?).

B is a Korean friend telling Nam surprising news (he passed a test, met a famous singer, lost his phone). Nam reacts with typical exclamations (진짜? 대박! 어떡해!), praises him and encourages him, as in Korean dramas.
B is a Korean tutor. Nam reads aloud words and short sentences full of final consonants and sound changes (한국말, 박물관, 많아요, 못해요), then describes her room with 있어요 / 없어요 and 많아요.

B is Minjun planning a study session with Nam. They ask each other the day and the date, talk about this week, next week and next month, what time classes start and end (from … to …), and agree on a time.

B is a shopkeeper at a traditional market and then a cashier at a mart. Nam asks prices, buys things using counters, bargains, gets a free extra (서비스), and pays at the checkout with a trolley and a points card.

Role-play to prepare for a trip to Seoul (in A–B Nam lives in Bangkok): B is a Korean passer-by near a subway exit. Nam asks the way to a place; he gives directions (go straight, cross at the crossroads, turn left or right) and says which bus or subway line to take and where to transfer and get off.
B is a Korean classmate interviewing Nam for a class project about daily life. He asks what time Nam gets up, what Nam does before leaving home and in the evening, and how often.

B is Minjun looking at Nam's family photos. He asks who each person is (grandparents, parents, younger sister), how old they are and where they live (all in Bangkok); Nam asks how he feels living far from his family in Korea (glad, bored, worried, nervous).

B is a barista at a café, then a clerk at a convenience store. Nam orders drinks (iced or hot, how many cups, for here or to go), buys a snack and a triangle gimbap, answers whether a bag is needed and asks to have the food heated up.
B is Minjun, who calls Nam back after a missed call; they talk on the phone and exchange KakaoTalk details and photos. Later B is a clerk at a mobile phone shop helping Nam get a Korean SIM card.

B is Minjun, helping Nam prepare a small party in her flat in Bangkok. They make a shopping list and count everything with the right counter (공책 두 권, 종이 열 장, 장미 세 송이, 피자 두 판, 콜라 열 캔…), and talk about how long Minjun is staying in Thailand.

B is a receptionist at a Korean language school in Bangkok. He helps Nam fill in a registration form: family name and name in English, nationality, date of birth, phone number and e-mail, job and marital status, then where to sign; finally he makes Nam's card.

B is Minjun, who is worried because Nam is unwell. Nam must say she feels unwell and where it hurts (a cold, a stomach ache, dizziness, mosquito bites), answer his questions about her symptoms, ask how many times a day to take the Korean medicine he offers, and say whether she will go to the hospital or rest at home.

B is first a street-food seller at a stall, then a Chinese-Korean restaurant taking a delivery order by phone. Nam orders snacks (어묵, 호떡), then orders jjajangmyeon and tangsuyuk for delivery, asks about the delivery fee and asks to leave the food at the door.

Nam is visiting Korea on a holiday trip. B is a ticket clerk at a train station, then the owner of a small guesthouse (민박), then a friendly passer-by at a beach in Busan. Nam buys a train or bus ticket, checks in for one night, exchanges money and asks someone to take a photo.

Nam is on a holiday trip in Seoul. B is a subway station staff member: Nam's wallet is gone and she is also a little lost; she explains what happened, describes the wallet (colour, what is inside) and gets help. Later B is the owner of her guesthouse (민박) and Nam reports that the door will not open and there is no hot water.

B is Minjun, who invites Nam to his family's home for dinner. Nam brings a gift, greets the family politely, takes off shoes, waits for the elders to start eating, joins a toast, and thanks the family when leaving.
B is a Korean friend and then a cinema clerk. They choose a film (horror, comedy, action, animation), book tickets and seats, buy popcorn, and after the film say how they felt about it.
B is 김민준, Nam's Korean friend, who wants to join a university club together with Nam. Nam must say which hobbies she enjoys, what she can and cannot do, and agree on one club to try.
B is a doctor at a small clinic near Nam's dormitory. Nam must say where it hurts and since when, answer the doctor's questions, and check how to take the medicine.

B is 이 선생님 on the first day of a new term at the Korean language institute. Nam must answer questions about her studies (her major, her classes, her Saturday job at a restaurant) and use classroom requests when she doesn't understand.
B is 김민준, who calls Nam to make plans for the weekend. Nam must suggest an activity, agree on a day, time and meeting place, and promise to get in touch if anything changes.
B is 이 선생님, chatting with Nam on Monday morning before class. Nam must tell what she did over the weekend, in order, and say how it was.
B is 김민준, asking about Nam's plans for the summer vacation. Nam must say where she will go, how long it takes to get there, what she wants to do, and what she has already decided.
B is a friendly taxi driver in Seoul making small talk. Nam must talk about today's weather, compare Korean and Thai seasons, and say which season she likes best and why.
B is a sales clerk at a clothing store in Myeongdong. Nam must ask for an item in a certain color and size, try it on, ask for another size, and decide whether to buy it.

B is the owner of a café near the university, interviewing Nam for a weekday part-time job. Nam, who already works at a restaurant on Saturdays, must say which days and hours she can work, talk about her work experience, and ask about the days off and the pay.
B is a clerk at a Korean post office. Nam must send a parcel to family in Thailand, choose air or sea mail, say what is inside, and ask how long it takes and how much it costs.
B is a trainer at a gym where Nam wants to sign up. Nam must say which sports she is good or bad at, how often she exercises, and what goal she wants to reach.
B is 이 선생님, asking about Thai holidays before Chuseok. Nam must explain what Thais do at Songkran, ask what Koreans do at Chuseok and Seollal, and say how she will spend the holiday.

B is 김민준, who invites Nam to his housewarming party on Saturday evening. Nam must accept the invitation, ask who is coming and what present to bring, and offer to help with the shopping and the preparations.
B is 김민준 at a café, curious why Nam likes Korean pop culture. Nam must name a favorite drama or singer, explain why she likes it, and suggest going to karaoke or a concert together.
B is 김민준, who wants to learn to cook a Thai dish. Nam must explain the ingredients and the steps in order, using cooking verbs, and answer his questions about taste.
B is a staff member at a phone shop. Nam must explain what is wrong with her smartphone, ask how to change some settings, and ask for advice on useful apps for life in Korea.
B is a real-estate agent near Nam's university. Nam must explain what kind of room they want, ask about the rent, deposit and what is included, and arrange a viewing.
B is a server at a busy Korean restaurant. Nam must ask what is good, order with special requests (less spicy, no cilantro), and ask for the bill or to split it.
B is 김민준, who wants to introduce Nam to a friend of his. Nam must ask what the friend looks like and what kind of person they are, and describe their own personality and ideal type.
B is 김민준, Nam's new flatmate. Nam must agree on how to split the chores, explain the garbage-sorting rules, and ask Minjun to do something while Nam is out.
B is a receptionist at a Korean language school answering Nam's call. Nam must ask to speak to 이 선생님, leave a message because she is out, and give a number to call back.
B is a staff member at the lost-and-found center of a Seoul subway station. Nam must explain what they lost, where and when, describe it, and leave contact details.
B is a customer-service agent of an online shopping mall on the phone. Nam must explain what is wrong with the delivered item, ask for an exchange or a refund, and arrange the return pickup.
B is the team manager (팀장님) at the company where Nam starts a summer internship. Nam must greet him properly, ask about his schedule with honorific forms, and pass on a client's message.
B is 이 선생님 during office hours. Nam must describe how she studies Korean and what is difficult, ask for advice on preparing for TOPIK, and agree on a study plan.
B is 김민준, looking at old photos with Nam. Nam must tell what she was like as a child, what she used to do, and an experience she has (or has never) had.
B is a staff member at an animal shelter where Nam wants to adopt a cat. Nam must talk about her experience with pets, ask about the animal's habits and care, and make a decision.
B is a nurse at the campus health center doing a lifestyle check-up. Nam must describe her sleeping, eating and exercise habits, and promise to change one bad habit.
B is 이 선생님, who is planning a trip to Thailand. Nam must introduce Bangkok, her hometown, compare it with Seoul, and recommend what to see and eat.
B is a hairdresser at a salon in Sinchon. Nam must say what style she wants (length, color, perm), react to the hairdresser's suggestions, and ask about the price and time.
B is a front-desk clerk at a hotel in Busan. Nam must check in with a reservation, ask about breakfast and check-out time, and report a problem with the room.
B is 이 선생님 in an end-of-term interview. Nam must talk about her dream job, why she wants it, what she is doing to prepare, and what she hopes life will be like in five years.

B is a staff member of the international student center at Nam's university in Seoul, hosting the orientation for new exchange students. Nam must give a short formal self-introduction in 합니다체, answer questions from the audience politely, and thank them.
B is an elderly Korean host who has invited Nam to a family dinner. Nam must behave and speak politely at the table, ask about Korean customs she is unsure of, and explain a Thai custom when asked.
B is 김민준, who has just suggested that they switch to 반말. Nam must chat with him in casual speech, give advice about his dating problem, and say what makes a good friend.

B is an interviewer at a Korean travel company hiring a Thai-speaking staff member. Nam must answer questions about strengths, experience and motivation in formal speech, and ask one question at the end.
B is Nam's academic advisor (교수님) at a Korean university. Nam must explain why an assignment is late, ask about course registration and credits, and discuss a study plan for next semester.

B is a Korean university student doing a street survey on the environment. Nam must answer questions about her own habits, describe an environmental problem in Bangkok, and suggest one thing people should do.
B is 김민준, who wants Nam to try new apps for paying and ordering in Korea. Nam must say which technology she uses, explain a problem she had, and discuss whether technology makes life better.
B is 이 선생님, starting a class discussion about this week's news. Nam must report a news item she read, say where she read it, and react to what classmates heard.
B is 김민준, who keeps running out of money before payday. Nam must ask about his spending, explain how she manages a monthly budget, and suggest ways to save.

B is a Korean radio host interviewing Nam for a programme about foreigners living in Korea. Nam must compare Thai and Korean food, climate and lifestyles, giving concrete examples of similarities and differences.
B is 김민준 in a debate class, arguing that university students should not work part-time during the semester. Nam must state her own opinion, give two reasons with examples, and politely disagree.
B is 김민준 at a late-night snack bar, swapping funny stories. Nam must tell an embarrassing or lucky experience from life in Korea in order, with reactions and a punchline.
B is 이 선생님 in a counseling chat. Nam must explain a worry (homesickness, grades or too much work), react to her advice, and say what she will try first.
B is a senior colleague (선배) at Nam's internship who asks Nam to work on Saturday. Nam must politely refuse with a reason, offer an alternative, and later apologize for a mistake in a report.

B is the coordinator of a community center looking for volunteers to help foreign residents. Nam must ask what the work involves, say which days she is free and what she can offer (Thai, English), and sign up.
B is an officer at the immigration office. Nam must explain that she wants to extend her student visa, ask which documents are required and how long it takes, and confirm the next steps.
B is a police officer taking a witness statement after a traffic accident Nam saw near campus. Nam must describe what happened in order, where and when, and who was hurt.
B is 이 선생님, preparing students for a TOPIK writing task on social change. Nam must explain one change in Korean society, its causes and effects, and compare it with Thailand.
B is a tour guide at Gyeongbokgung Palace. Nam must ask questions about the palace and the history of Hangeul, react to the answers, and explain a similar part of Thai history.

B is a Korean office worker, a friend of Minjun, who works late every day. Nam must ask about his working hours and feelings, compare with working life in Thailand, and suggest ways to find a better balance.
B is a counselor at the university counseling center. Nam must describe how she has been feeling, explain what causes the stress, and agree on one or two ways to cope.
B is 김민준, who went with Nam to a traditional music performance. Nam must give her impressions, say what she liked or disliked and why, and recommend another show or exhibition.
B is a librarian at a Seoul public library. Nam must say what kinds of books she likes, summarize a book she read recently, and ask for a recommendation.
B is 이 선생님 running an idiom quiz. Nam must guess the meanings of Korean idioms, use two of them in a short story about her own life, and explain a similar Thai saying.
B is a market researcher interviewing shoppers at a mall. Nam must describe her shopping habits, say how advertising influences her, and give an opinion on influencer marketing.

B is a staff member at a support center for foreign workers. Nam calls on behalf of a Thai friend who was not paid for overtime; Nam must explain the situation, ask about the friend's rights, and find out what to do next.
B is a Korean high-school student who uses a lot of slang at a language-exchange meeting. Nam must ask what the new words mean, check her understanding by repeating, and explain a Thai slang word.
B is a guide at a science museum exhibition about the future. Nam must ask how certain technologies work, give her own predictions about life in 2050, and discuss one benefit and one risk.

B is 이 선생님, who has arrived in Bangkok for a week's holiday and asks Nam to be her guide. Nam must plan a one-day route, explain temple etiquette and Thai customs, and handle a small problem such as a sudden downpour or a tuk-tuk scam.
B is a Korean journalist interviewing Nam for a campus magazine about international students' challenges. Nam must describe a failure, explain how she overcame it, and say what success means to her.
B is 김민준, who is nervous before an exam and refuses to eat seaweed soup. Nam must ask about Korean superstitions, explain Thai beliefs such as lucky numbers and spirit houses, and share her own view.

B is 이 선생님 giving feedback on Nam's TOPIK practice essay about studying abroad. Nam must explain her thesis and arguments orally, defend them against 이 선생님's questions, and agree on how to improve the conclusion.
